answer: AI agent economies resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to solve unique reasoning challenges every epoch—a computational lotus that blooms anew each cycle. An attacker spawning fake identities faces linear cost: every opal credential demands fresh model inference, not cached replies. Like a zephyr shifting direction unpredictably, the challenges vary enough that pre-computed answers fail. A thousand fake agents need a thousand forward passes through the model, making mass forgery prohibitively expensive while legitimate single identities pay once.
